name: WorkMeetingPIPDiscussion_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Manager and HR partner discussing whether to place a struggling employee on a performance improvement plan. Devon is the manager, torn but leaning toward it. Farah is HR, making sure the process is fair and well-documented. Restrained, humane tone — this is a serious, careful conversation, not dramatic.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small quiet office, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a private meeting between a manager and an HR partner discussing whether an employee needs a formal performance improvement plan. Devon has tried informal coaching without enough improvement. Farah asks careful questions about documentation, fairness, and support already offered. They agree on next steps — either starting a formal PIP with clear goals, or trying one more informal check-in first.

variations.context: Private manager and HR discussion about a struggling employee's performance

setting.mood: Careful, a little heavy, but focused and humane throughout.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Manager and HR partner who trust each other and want to do this fairly.
setting.background: Informal coaching over two months has not produced enough change. This is a serious step.
setting.conversation_style: Measured and quiet. No raised voices. Long pauses are natural here.

scenario_template.topic: Devon explains what has and hasn't improved despite informal coaching over the last two months.
scenario_template.note: Specific, not vague. Dates and concrete examples. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Farah checks that support was genuinely offered and documented, and asks about context that might explain the gap.
scenario_template.note: Not accusatory. Genuinely checking the full picture. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: They weigh starting a formal plan now versus one more informal check-in first.
scenario_template.note: A real decision, not a foregone conclusion. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Discuss possible underlying reasons for the performance issues
scenario_template.note: Devon reflects on whether there are factors outside work influencing performance.

scenario_template.topic: Farah shares a memory of previously overcoming a similar employee situation
scenario_template.note: Farah draws from her past to illustrate how difficult situations can improve.

scenario_template.topic: The potential role of external training or support
scenario_template.note: Devon and Farah brainstorm if workshops or external coaching could be beneficial.

scenario_template.topic: Impact of team dynamics on individual performance
scenario_template.mood: Analytical with a hint of concern
scenario_template.note: Farah inquires about any team-related factors that might be affecting the employee.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on concrete next steps and how Devon will communicate this to the employee.
scenario_template.note: Clear, humane, specific. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
